official_sources.title: GDAL natural block size and exact edge-block dimensions
official_sources.finding: GDAL exposes each band's natural block size and the actual valid width and height of partial right or bottom edge blocks; ReadBlock reads a natural block without resampling or data-type conversion.
official_sources.limitation: Bytes outside the valid extent of a partial edge block are unspecified and must never enter the parcel mask or extrema reduction.

official_sources.title: GDAL suggested block access pattern
official_sources.finding: GDAL exposes a suggested block access pattern and documents block-boundary reads as the highest-performance full-resolution access path.
official_sources.limitation: A performance suggestion does not define result order; the application must still assign a canonical block sequence independent of driver hints.

official_sources.title: GDAL raster read-only thread-safe dataset RFC 101
official_sources.finding: GDAL 3.10 adds read-only raster dataset wrappers that are safe for calls from multiple threads and internally use a dataset instance per thread.
official_sources.limitation: Thread safety prevents unsafe shared-state access but does not guarantee deterministic completion order, reduction order or identical cache behavior.

official_sources.title: GDAL multi-threading and block-cache constraints
official_sources.finding: GDAL generally requires distinct dataset instances per thread unless a thread-safe read-only wrapper is used, and warns that related raster bands from one ordinary dataset must not be called concurrently.
official_sources.limitation: Global and per-thread cache behavior can change performance and resource use; cache state must not alter accepted cell bytes or ordering.

official_sources.title: Rasterio block windows and native block-aligned reads
official_sources.finding: Rasterio documents that raster I/O occurs in dataset blocks and windowed reads are most efficient when windows match the source block structure.
official_sources.limitation: The iterable order of produced work must be persisted explicitly rather than inferred from asynchronous task completion.

official_sources.title: Rasterio concurrent window processing pattern
official_sources.finding: Rasterio releases the GIL around GDALRasterIO and shows block-window processing with thread pools while protecting shared dataset reads and writes with locks.
official_sources.limitation: Concurrency examples target safe and faster processing, not deterministic extrema aggregation; result collection must be keyed by canonical block index.

official_sources.title: Python Future completion-order semantics
official_sources.finding: Python concurrent futures provides submission-order map results and completion-order iteration through as_completed, so collection strategy can change observed result order.
official_sources.limitation: A deterministic computation must not let worker timing choose which equal extrema location or diagnostic record is retained.

official_sources.title: NumPy first-occurrence extrema and stable multi-key ordering
official_sources.finding: NumPy argmin and argmax return only the first occurrence of an extreme, while stable indirect sorting tools can preserve deterministic ordering across explicit keys.
official_sources.limitation: The meaning of first depends on array layout and merge order; all tied cells must be enumerated before selecting any canonical representative.
